sourcing_notes:
WHAT I REACHED. (1) https://openai.com/news/rss.xml - HTTP 200, 725,972 bytes, 1,194 <item>, newest pubDate Wed, 16 Sep 2026 13:00:00 GMT. Live and official. Each item carries OpenAI's own one-line description, and those descriptions contain real figures ('31 European markets', '$1 billion in annualized revenue run rate'). There is no <content:encoded>; the feed exposes title, description, link, guid, category, pubDate only. (2) developers.openai.com - NOT blocked. This is the important new finding. Its sitemap (https://developers.openai.com/sitemap-index.xml -> /sitemap-0.xml, 1,315 URLs) lists 31 official ChatGPT Ads documentation pages under https://developers.openai.com/ads/. All 31 returned HTTP 200 as HTML and as the Markdown twin the site itself advertises ('Markdown versions of documentation pages are available by appending .md to the page URL'). Also reachable: https://developers.openai.com/ads/llms-full.txt (HTTP 200, 355,929 bytes, single-file export) and https://developers.openai.com/ads/openapi.json (HTTP 200, OpenAPI 3.1.0, info.version 2.3.0, 64 paths, servers[0].url https://api.ads.openai.com/v1). (3) https://openai.com/robots.txt and https://openai.com/sitemap.xml plus its 38 sub-sitemaps return HTTP 200 even though every HTML page on openai.com returns 403 - useful for confirming canonical URLs and lastmod dates without guessing.

WHAT I COULD NOT REACH, with the status actually observed. https://openai.com/index/new-ways-to-buy-chatgpt-ads/ -> HTTP 403, response header 'cf-mitigated: challenge', server: cloudflare, body is the Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' interstitial. Same 403 for the other ads posts, for locale variants (/ja-JP/index/...), for ?_rsc=, for /policies/ad-policies/, /policies/ad-tools-terms/, /policies/row-privacy-policy/, /news/, /chatgpt/, /llms.txt. help.openai.com: robots.txt is 200 but every article is 403 with cf-mitigated: challenge, including the two article URLs the repo's existing pack cites (en/articles/20001047-ads-in-chatgpt, en-us/articles/20001245-ads-manager-availability). https://ads.openai.com/ -> 403 Cloudflare challenge (reached via a 302 from https://chatgpt.com/ads, so the hostname is confirmed, not guessed). https://developers.openai.com/ads/openai-geotargets.csv -> redirects to https://ads.openai.com/assets/openai-geotargets.csv and therefore 403, so the official list of targetable countries/regions/markets could not be read. https://chatgpt.com/sitemap.xml and /marketing-sitemap.xml -> 403. https://advertising.openai.com -> connect failure (proxy 502).

WHY 'partial'. The assignment's angle has two halves. How the ads are sold is fully documented from a first-party surface I actually fetched. What OpenAI states about privacy separation lives almost entirely on openai.com/index/* and help.openai.com, both 403; the only privacy wording I can quote is OpenAI's own one-line feed descriptions. An article can be written, but it must be built around the buying mechanism and must attribute every privacy sentence to OpenAI's feed wording, not to an article body nobody here has read.

SOURCES LIST vs EXTRA URLS. The four entries in `sources` are the ones the writer should cite. I also fetched and recorded facts from sibling doc pages that are NOT in the four; those facts are tagged '[NOT IN sources]'. To use one, swap it into the four-source list; never cite a URL that is not in the pack's sources.

verified_facts.fact: The self-serve product is called Ads Manager and lives at https://ads.openai.com/. OpenAI's docs say you need an ad account there, and that the Advertiser API key is created on the Settings page inside Ads Manager (https://ads.openai.com/settings). verified_facts.fact: Buying is structured in four levels: Ad account contains Campaigns, each Campaign contains Ad groups, each Ad group contains Ads. The docs state exactly what is configured where: Ad account = advertiser branding, currency, timezone, account access, spend limits; Campaign = objective, budget, schedule, geographic and platform targeting, audience inclusion and exclusion, conversion events; Ad group = bid strategy, context hints, audience bid multipliers, product set; Ad = creative, image or product template, destination URL.

The Advertiser API base URL is https://api.ads.openai.com and authentication is a bearer token ('Authorization: Bearer ...'). Supported create endpoints accept an Idempotency-Key so a network retry does not create a duplicate.

An ad creative in the worked example is of type 'chat_card' and carries a title, a body, a target_url and an uploaded image file_id. The uploaded creative image must be at least 640 x 640 pixels. Creating an ad submits its creative for review.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Use an image at least 640 × 640 pixels.

verified_facts.fact: Newly created campaigns, ad groups and ads are created paused in the documented workflow, and each level has to be activated separately (/ads/{id}/activate, /ad_groups/{id}/activate, /campaigns/{id}/activate). The docs are explicit that activation is not sufficient: 'Activation enables delivery when the remaining requirements are satisfied.' A preview shows appearance only: 'A preview shows appearance; it does not confirm serving eligibility.'
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: A preview shows appearance; it does not confirm serving eligibility.

verified_facts.fact: Advertiser API rate limits are published: 600 requests per minute per endpoint and 1,200 requests per minute overall, enforced by both ad account and IP address. Bulk job creation has a separate limit of 10 requests per 10 seconds per ad account.

The Ads API changelog on this page has dated entries only from 3 June 2026 onward. In order: September 10th, 2026 - granular web platform targeting with desktop_web, ios_web and android_web; September 9th, 2026 - daily account spending limits for ad accounts on postpaid invoice billing, renewing at midnight in the account timezone; August 25th, 2026 - custom audience Add, Remove, Replace and Merge operations, automatic identifier matching, and support for small and empty exclusion-only audiences; July 16th, 2026 - passing the Pixel browser reference as events[].user.obref in Conversions API requests; June 16th, 2026 - conversion-optimized campaign bidding with bidding_type 'conversions'; June 11th, 2026 - segmented insights for product, country and device breakdowns plus zero-impression product expansion; June 3rd, 2026 - location targeting including /geo_lookup/search, plus conversion setup and reporting endpoints for API keys, pixels, event settings and conversion insights. The only entry before those is an undated 'v1 - Published the initial API version'. THE CHANGELOG DOES NOT DATE THE 2026-05-05 ANNOUNCEMENT AND DOES NOT MENTION THE SELF-SERVE ADS MANAGER BETA.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote:
### v1

- Published the initial API version.

verified_facts.fact: There are exactly three campaign objectives and they determine what the advertiser pays for. The docs table: bidding_type 'impressions' with billing_event_type 'impression' and strategy 'fixed_bid'; bidding_type 'clicks' with billing_event_type 'click' and strategy 'fixed_bid' or 'maximize_clicks'; bidding_type 'conversions' with billing_event_type 'click' and strategy 'fixed_bid' or 'maximize_conversions'. So paying per click (CPC) is the billing event for both the clicks objective and the conversions objective.

The campaign objective and the budget sit on the campaign; the billing event and the bid strategy sit on the ad group. The docs state it as a table: 'Campaign objective | Campaign | The outcome to optimize for'; 'Campaign budget | Campaign | The daily or lifetime spending limit shared by its ad groups'; 'Billing event | Ad group | Whether you pay for impressions or clicks'; 'Bid strategy | Ad group | Whether you set bids or let OpenAI adjust them'.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Billing event | Ad group | Whether you pay for impressions or clicks

verified_facts.fact: Three bid strategies are documented. Fixed bid: the advertiser sets the bid via max_bid_micros, works with impressions, clicks or conversions objectives, and with a daily or lifetime budget. Maximize clicks: OpenAI adjusts bids to seek more clicks from the budget, clicks objective only, daily budget only, max_bid_micros omitted. Maximize conversions: same but for the conversions objective. OpenAI names the latter two collectively 'Maximize Results', and says both are available for standard and product-feed campaigns.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: **Maximize Results** is the name for the `maximize_clicks` and `maximize_conversions` strategies.

verified_facts.fact: Bids and budgets are integers in micros: one major currency unit equals 1,000,000 micros. The docs' worked USD examples: $1.00 = 1000000; $2.50 = 2500000; $50.00 = 50000000; a $2 click bid = 2000000; a $3 click bid = 3000000; a $50 daily budget = 50000000; a $500 lifetime budget = 500000000; an updated $75 daily budget = 75000000; a $200 daily budget on the conversion example = 200000000. For impression bidding the API expects a bid PER IMPRESSION, so a $60 CPM is $0.06 per impression = 60000 micros. All of these are labelled illustrative amounts in the docs, not prices OpenAI charges.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: A $60 CPM bid is $0.06 per impression, so send `60000` micros: `60 ÷ 1,000 × 1,000,000 = 60000`.

verified_facts.fact: A campaign has exactly one budget field, daily_spend_limit_micros or lifetime_spend_limit_micros, never both. Maximize Results requires a daily budget. A lifetime budget cannot be reduced below what the campaign has already spent, and a daily budget cannot be switched back to a lifetime budget through an update - you have to create a new campaign.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: You cannot switch a daily budget back to a lifetime budget through a campaign update.

verified_facts.fact: OpenAI does not publish the minimum spend. The docs say only: 'Daily minimums depend on the account currency. Requests below the applicable minimum return an error with the required amount.' and 'Bid limits and permitted monetary precision depend on the account currency and campaign objective.' No number is given anywhere on the page.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Daily minimums depend on the account currency. Requests below the applicable minimum return an error with the required amount.

verified_facts.fact: The API can tell an advertiser its bid may be too low, but explicitly refuses to treat that as a block: requesting include[]=bid_too_low returns guidance only. 'bid_too_low: true indicates that the bid may be too low for reliable delivery. It is guidance, not a serving restriction.'
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: It is guidance, not a serving restriction.

verified_facts.fact: Money spent is gated at two independent levels. 'Campaign budgets and ad account spend limits apply independently. Raising a campaign budget does not override an exhausted account spend limit.' Account spend-limit windows are not universal: 'Spend-limit windows are available only to some accounts.'
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Spend-limit windows are available only to some accounts.

verified_facts.fact: Whether an ad actually shows depends on more than budget and bid. The docs list the conditions: 'Delivery also depends on the campaign schedule, resource statuses, reviews, targeting, and available inventory.'
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Delivery also depends on the campaign schedule, resource statuses, reviews, targeting, and available inventory.

verified_facts.fact: Targeting decides who is eligible to see a campaign's ads, and the three kinds stack rather than override each other: 'Campaign targeting determines who is eligible to receive the campaign's ads. Geographic, platform, and audience settings work together; matching one setting does not override the others.' Exclusions win over inclusions when someone is in both.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Exclusions take precedence when someone belongs to both an included audience and an excluded audience.

verified_facts.fact: Geographic targeting uses ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes or location IDs from /geo_lookup/search, and OpenAI warns that a valid country code is not the same as an available advertising country. This is the sentence to use instead of speculating about Taiwan: 'A code's ISO validity does not mean it is available for advertising in your account; use supported advertising locations.'
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: A code’s ISO validity does not mean it is available for advertising in your account; use supported advertising locations.

verified_facts.fact: Platform targeting picks which ChatGPT surfaces an ad can appear on, and the docs spell out a counter-intuitive case: 'This selects the web group. It does not mean desktop-only traffic. An iPhone user visiting ChatGPT in a browser belongs to web inventory rather than the iOS app group.'
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: An iPhone user visiting ChatGPT in a browser belongs to web inventory rather than the iOS app group.

verified_facts.fact: The mechanism that links an ad to what a user is talking about is called Context Hints, set on the ad group. Advertisers write free-text descriptions of the product or use case - the docs' own examples are 'Lightweight trail running shoes for rocky terrain' and 'Water-resistant footwear for wet-weather hiking'. An ad group can contain up to 2,000 hints. OpenAI states two limits on them: 'Hints are not exact-match keywords. They also do not replace explicit geographic, platform, or audience targeting.'
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Hints are not exact-match keywords. They also do not replace explicit geographic, platform, or audience targeting.

verified_facts.fact: This is the single most useful sentence for the reader angle, and it is a disclaimer rather than a promise: OpenAI will not guarantee that writing a particular hint makes an ad appear in a particular conversation. It is also the only place in the whole ads documentation set that uses the word 'conversation' in relation to ad triggering.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: These examples illustrate writing style, not a guarantee that a particular conversation will trigger an ad.

verified_facts.fact: Advertisers can upload customer lists as custom audiences, and there is a documented floor: 'Inclusion and bid multipliers require at least 25,000 matched users; exclusion audiences have no minimum matched count.' Including an audience restricts eligibility to matching users; a bid multiplier only changes the bid for them and leaves non-members eligible.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Inclusion and bid multipliers require at least 25,000 matched users; exclusion audiences have no minimum matched count.

verified_facts.fact: [NOT IN sources - https://developers.openai.com/ads/custom-audiences] Personalised ads are stated as not yet available in part of Europe: 'Custom audiences are not supported for campaigns targeting the European Economic Area (EEA) or Switzerland, where personalized ads are not yet available.' The same page requires advertisers to upload only first-party data they have the right to use, forbids broker-sourced data, and points at OpenAI's Ad Tools Terms (https://openai.com/policies/ad-tools-terms/, which returns 403 here).
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Custom audiences are not supported for campaigns targeting the European Economic Area (EEA) or Switzerland, where personalized ads are not yet available.

verified_facts.fact: [NOT IN sources - https://developers.openai.com/ads/conversion-optimized-campaigns] Conversion-optimised CPC (oCPC) is described as open beta for standard and product-feed campaigns, and the billing stays per click: 'Billing does not change to pay per conversion. OpenAI charges you only when a valid click occurs, and the auction determines the actual CPC.' The three goals are tabulated as impressions (CPM, per 1,000 impressions), clicks (CPC, per valid click) and conversions (oCPC, per valid click, not per conversion). An existing CPM or CPC campaign cannot be converted to oCPC, and the selected conversion event cannot be changed after creation.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Billing does not change to pay per conversion. OpenAI charges you only when a valid click occurs, and the auction determines the actual CPC.

verified_facts.fact: [NOT IN sources - https://developers.openai.com/ads/conversion-tracking] Measurement has two documented routes that share a Pixel ID: a browser JavaScript Measurement Pixel and a server-to-server Conversions API. 'Both integrations use a Pixel ID to identify the data source. A server-only integration still needs a Pixel ID, but does not require installing the browser Pixel.'
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: A server-only integration still needs a Pixel ID, but does not require installing the browser Pixel.

verified_facts.fact: [NOT IN sources - https://developers.openai.com/ads/measurement-pixel] The Measurement Pixel SDK is loaded from https://bzrcdn.openai.com/sdk/oaiq.min.js and initialised with a Pixel ID created in the conversions tab of Ads Manager. It supports a consent gate - oaiq('consent', false) before init, oaiq('consent', true) after the user grants measurement consent - and a per-event opt_out option described as 'Set to true to opt out the event from future user-level personalization.' The SDK automatically captures an identifier called oppref from the landing page URL, described as 'a privacy-preserving identifier', and stores it in a first-party __oppref cookie. When automatic advanced matching is enabled it hashes detected customer information with SHA-256 before sending it.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: It captures `oppref` from the landing page URL, which is a privacy-preserving identifier

verified_facts.fact: [NOT IN sources - https://developers.openai.com/ads/measurement-pixel] View-through conversions use a fixed one-day window after an eligible ad impression, are reported in Ads Manager as a separate campaign-level metric, and are deliberately excluded from the main Conversions total. 'CPA, post-click CVR, bidding, billing, and conversion optimization also remain click-through-based.' Where a conversion qualifies for both, the click takes precedence.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: View-through conversions use a fixed one-day window after an eligible ad impression.

verified_facts.fact: [NOT IN sources - https://developers.openai.com/ads/supported-events] Thirteen conversion event names are documented: app_installed, app_opened, appointment_scheduled, checkout_started, contents_viewed, custom, items_added, lead_created, order_created, page_viewed, registration_completed, subscription_created, trial_started. app_installed and app_opened are Conversions API only and are not supported by the JavaScript Pixel. Monetary values are sent as integers in the ISO 4217 minor unit, e.g. 12999 for $129.99 with currency USD.

[NOT IN sources - https://developers.openai.com/ads/reporting] The reported metrics are impressions, clicks, spend, ctr, cpc, cpm, conversions, cpa, post_click_cvr, order_created_attributed_sales and order_created_roas. CTR is returned as a ratio (0.04 means 4%). Spend, CPC and CPM are in major currency units, not micros. The docs warn that 'A null value means the metric is unavailable or cannot be calculated. It does not mean zero.'
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: A `null` value means the metric is unavailable or cannot be calculated. It does not mean zero.

verified_facts.fact: [NOT IN sources - https://developers.openai.com/ads/api-reference/ads] Creative text is tightly capped: creative.title is 3 to 50 characters and creative.body is at most 100 characters. Every ad carries a review_status of in_review, rejected or approved, and a rejected ad is said to violate OpenAI's ads policies (linked as https://openai.com/policies/ad-policies/, which returns 403 here). An ad preview expires 24 hours after creation. The two creative types are chat_card and product_ad_template.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: `creative.title` | string | Yes | `3` to `50` chars.

verified_facts.fact: [NOT IN sources - https://developers.openai.com/ads/bulk-api] OpenAI uses the term 'self-serve' as an official limit category: 5,000 non-archived self-serve campaigns per ad account, 5,000 non-archived self-serve ad groups, and 5,000 active or paused self-serve ads.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Self-serve campaigns per ad account | `5,000` non-archived campaigns

verified_facts.fact: [NOT IN sources - https://developers.openai.com/ads/openapi.json] The machine-readable spec confirms the enumerations rather than leaving them to prose: campaign bidding_type is one of impressions, clicks, conversions; billing_event_type is one of impression, click; ad-group bidding strategy is one of fixed_bid, maximize_clicks, maximize_conversions (the response schema also carries automated_bid). The spec declares OpenAPI 3.1.0, info.version 2.3.0, 64 paths, server https://api.ads.openai.com/v1.

overlaps_existing_article:
SERIOUS OVERLAP - the parent should decide whether this article should exist at all before a writer starts. apps/api/app/guides/content/chatgpt-ads-status.json already exists: slug chatgpt-ads-status, kind life, topics ['tutorial','ai-chat'], display_order 100, zh-TW only, 33 blocks, no summary and no faq, checked 2026-09-14, titled 'ChatGPT 廣告怎麼查：開放地區、官方規則與品牌準備'. It cites https://openai.com/index/new-ways-to-buy-chatgpt-ads/ as one of its five sources, and its final section already summarises exactly this event: CPC 點擊出價、自助管理工具、Conversions API 與像素量測. It also already covers advertiser-country availability (and that Taiwan was not on the list on 2026-09-14), the 8/18 Europe expansion and the 31 markets, labelling and separation from answers, which plans see ads, aggregated measurement, and the ad policies. Note that ai.md's table of 38 existing titles lists only ai-news-* slugs, so it does not surface this pack - which is why the candidate list treats 2026-05-05 as an untouched gap.

IF THE ARTICLE IS STILL WANTED, divide it like this. chatgpt-ads-status keeps the brand-preparation angle: am I eligible, what do I prepare, what do I check on the official pages. The new ai-news piece must be event-anchored and mechanism-focused, and must add what the existing pack does not have: the four-level structure (ad account / campaign / ad group / ad) and what is set at each level; the three objectives and what each one actually bills for (CPM per 1,000 impressions, CPC per valid click, oCPC still per valid click); fixed bid versus Maximize Results and which budget type each needs; micros; the Context Hints mechanism and OpenAI's refusal to guarantee that a hint triggers an ad in any particular conversation; platform targeting and the web-versus-app inventory quirk; the 25,000 matched-user floor for audience inclusion; and the dated Ads API changelog from 2026-06-03 to 2026-09-10, which shows the product still moving four months after the announcement. The second link block should point at chatgpt-ads-status so the two do not compete, and the article should not repeat its eligibility checklist.

Also weigh the freshness problem: OpenAI published another ads post on the check date itself (2026-09-16, 'Reimagining advertising with AI'), and the Europe and milestone posts were both revised on 2026-09-16. An article pinned to 2026-05-05 is the fourth event in a six-event line.
editorial_brief:
讀者是台灣的一般 ChatGPT 使用者，不是廣告代理商。他們開始在對話裡看到或聽說有廣告，想知道「我看到的東西是怎麼來的」。切入點是賣方的機制：2026 年 5 月 5 日 OpenAI 在自家新聞渠道宣布「New ways to buy ChatGPT ads」，官方描述提到 beta 自助式 Ads Manager、CPC 出價與量測工具；一個廣告主要先建廣告帳戶、再建廣告活動（決定目標、預算、地區與平台）、廣告組（決定出價方式與 context hints）、才是真正的廣告素材，而且每一層都要通過審核才能上線。重點要把「按曝光付費」、「按點擊付費」、「以轉換為目標但仍按點擊付費」三件事分開講，因為這決定了廣告主想要使用者做什麼。

第二個重點是界線：本站只能讀到 OpenAI 官方 feed 的一句話描述與廣告 API 文件，宣布原文與說明中心在本容器回 403。所以「廣告與對話分開」、「清楚標示」這些話一律寫成「OpenAI 在官方說明裡表示」，並明說本文沒有登入廣告後台、沒有實測。最有價值的一句官方原文反而是免責性質的：官方文件寫明 context hints 的範例「是寫法示範，不保證某一段對話會觸發廣告」。

生活情境由編輯自行設計並標明為例子（例如一位使用者在問登山鞋，廣告主寫的是「岩地輕量越野鞋」這種描述），不得寫成實際案例。

這篇刻意不談：台灣能不能看到或買到廣告（查不到一手來源）、哪些方案會出現廣告（來源被擋）、最低預算與實際廣告費（官方未公佈）、以及廣告主的準備步驟（由現有的 chatgpt-ads-status 負責）。結尾的 callout 講查證日與可用性的區別；相關新聞連結指向 chatgpt-ads-status。

NEW BLOCKS to record so nobody rediscovers them: https://ads.openai.com/ returns 403 Cloudflare challenge on every path including robots.txt and sitemap.xml (https://chatgpt.com/ads 302-redirects there, which is how the hostname was confirmed). https://developers.openai.com/ads/openai-geotargets.csv redirects to ads.openai.com/assets/ and therefore 403s, so the official targetable-location catalogue is unreadable. https://chatgpt.com/sitemap.xml and /marketing-sitemap.xml are 403. https://advertising.openai.com does not resolve (proxy 502). openai.com/llms.txt is 403.

Refine the openai.com block description: it is not WebFetch-specific. curl with -A Mokaair-editorial gets HTTP 403 with response headers 'cf-mitigated: challenge' and 'server: cloudflare' and a JavaScript interstitial body. Locale prefixes (/ja-JP/, /de-DE/) and query variants do not help. XML and txt paths under openai.com are the exception and do return 200.

help.openai.com is confirmed 403 for articles, but its /robots.txt returns 200 (it is an Intercom-style help centre with Crawl-delay: 1 and only /not-authorized and /not-found disallowed). Do not read the 200 on robots.txt as the help centre being reachable.
